title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Choose ten distinct study environments. Verify access rules, room or reservation constraints, and the physical affordance that makes each useful. Treat “Claimed by 9am” as editorial framing; never assert crowding or student behavior without evidence.

cards.title: The Main Library Stacks
cards.subtitle: Educational Resources Center (ERC)
cards.notes: Access the back room stacks for quiet individual study. Use the iPad touchscreens on the columns to locate specific reference materials or technical reports.
cards.short_summary: The primary quiet study area located within the Educational Resources Center on the hill campus.
cards.evidence_claim: The Harriet Call Burnap Memorial Library is the main library located in the Educational Resources Center and offers reference materials and books for checkout.
cards.access_notes: Open daily; check library website for specific reference desk and stack access hours.

cards.title: The Forum Stairwell
cards.subtitle: Student Center Ground Floor
cards.notes: Utilize this innovative stairwell auditorium for casual study between classes. It features a massive video wall and comfortable seating for individuals or groups.
cards.short_summary: A tiered, open-concept seating area in the Student Center used for both events and informal studying.
cards.evidence_claim: The Forum is an innovative auditorium in the form of a stairwell equipped with a massive video wall, used for study and meetings.
cards.source_title: Clarkson University Student Center Tour - YouTube
cards.access_notes: Open during Student Center hours; may be reserved for large lectures or performances.

cards.title: Collaborative Reservation Suites
cards.subtitle: Educational Resources Center
cards.notes: Book these rooms through the University EMS system for group projects. Each room features an iPad display showing the current reservation schedule.
cards.short_summary: Reservable group spaces in the ERC designed for collaboration, presentation rehearsal, and digital creation.
cards.evidence_claim: Spaces in the ERC are available for reservation through the University EMS system for group collaboration and presentation rehearsal.
cards.access_notes: Reservations required via EMS; priority given to groups using rooms for intended purposes.

cards.title: MoJoe Coffee Lounge
cards.subtitle: Snell Hall First Floor
cards.notes: Study in a social atmosphere near MoJoe Coffee. This space is ideal for School of Business students needing a quick caffeine break between sessions.
cards.short_summary: A cafe-adjacent study area within the 92,000 square foot Snell Hall academic building.
cards.evidence_claim: Snell Hall features areas for conference rooms, MoJoe Coffee, and classrooms designed for distance learning.
cards.source_title: A Look Inside Bertrand H. Snell Hall at Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Publicly accessible during building hours; coffee purchase is optional for seating use.

cards.title: The CAMP Atrium
cards.subtitle: CAMP Building Entrance
cards.notes: Find seating in the large atrium near the main oval drive entrance. It provides a modern, bright environment for engineering and science students.
cards.short_summary: A spacious, sunlit atrium located at the entrance of the CAMP research and classroom facility.
cards.evidence_claim: The CAMP building features a main entrance with an atrium located on the left as you walk toward the back lecture halls.
cards.source_title: SOAR Location Detail: Clarkson University: CAMP 175
cards.access_notes: Open during academic building hours; typically quietest during late afternoon lab sessions.

cards.title: Commuter Study Lounge
cards.subtitle: ERC First Floor
cards.notes: Use this dedicated space designed specifically for students who live off-campus. It is located near the commuter lockers and academic support offices.
cards.short_summary: A specialized study area for commuter students to use between classes or during weekends.
cards.evidence_claim: Potsdam commuter students have access to a dedicated study space at the Student Success Center.
cards.access_notes: Available to all students, with a focus on supporting the commuter population.

cards.title: The Downtown Book Room
cards.subtitle: Clarkson Hall (Downtown Campus)
cards.notes: Visit the downtown campus for a change of scenery. This library supports graduate health programs and offers a quiet environment for focused reading.
cards.short_summary: A branch library located downtown in Clarkson Hall, serving health sciences programs.
cards.evidence_claim: The Health Sciences Library is located downtown in Clarkson Hall and supports graduate health sciences programs.
cards.access_notes: Restricted hours; the Book Room is only open when the library is staffed.

cards.entity_name: Cora and Bayard Clarkson Science Center
cards.title: The Purple Couch Lounge
cards.subtitle: Science Center Corridor
cards.notes: Relax on the signature purple couches at the end of the corridor. This lounge area is situated where the main hallway meets the back wing of the building.
cards.short_summary: A casual lounge area with distinctive purple seating located within the Science Center.
cards.evidence_claim: A lounge area with purple couches is located where the end of the corridor meets the corner of the building near room 175.
cards.source_title: SOAR Location Detail: Clarkson University: CAMP 175
cards.access_notes: Open during Science Center building hours; popular for quick breaks between labs.

cards.title: 24/7 TAC Workstations
cards.subtitle: Technology Advancement Center
cards.notes: Access high-speed network workstations in this modern facility. The building is designed to support advanced research and technical learning platforms.
cards.short_summary: A technology-focused study space with 24/7 computer lab access for students.
cards.evidence_claim: Clarkson has computer labs available 24/7, including workstations connected to the high-speed network backbone.
cards.source_title: Office of Information Technology | Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: 24/7 access available with student ID card swipe.

cards.title: The Living Room Lounge
cards.subtitle: Student Center Level 2
cards.notes: Study in the 'living room' of campus with comfortable chairs and tables. This area is reservable for student groups but open for individual use when empty.
cards.short_summary: A comfortable, multi-purpose lounge area on the second floor of the Student Center.
cards.evidence_claim: The Student Center features a variety of lounges and spaces with comfortable chairs and tables for studying and relaxing.
cards.source_title: OSL - Student Center Use Policy | Clarkson University
cards.access_notes: Open during Student Center hours; check for group reservation notices on the door.
